text: Same meaning
Some words are near twins: they mean almost the same thing. Big and large. Quick and fast.
{A} means about the same as {B}.
Swap one word for the other in a sentence. If the sentence still means the same, they are twins.
Watch for a word that goes WITH the word but does not MEAN it. Cool and breeze go together, but a breeze is not cool.
Opposites
Opposites sit at the two ends of the same line. Hot and cold are both about temperature, at opposite ends.
{A} is the opposite of {B}.
Ask: are they about the same thing, at opposite ends? Full and empty are both about how much is inside.
A near twin is the most tempting wrong answer here. If you need the opposite of happy, glad is a trap: it means the same.
Kind of
Some pairs are a member and its group. A robin is a kind of bird. An oak is a kind of tree.
{A} is a kind of {B}.
Say "is a kind of" between the two words. If it sounds right, you have found the link.
Another member of the same group is a trap. For robin, sparrow tempts you, but a sparrow is not the group. And watch the direction: a bird is not a kind of robin.

what: analogy lesson “Part of a whole”, its title
text: Part of a whole

what: analogy lesson “Part of a whole”, its idea
text: Some pairs are a piece and the thing it belongs to. A petal is part of a flower. A page is part of a book.

what: analogy lesson “Part of a whole”, its bridge
text: {A} is part of {B}.

what: analogy lesson “Part of a whole”, its spot
text: Ask: could you find the first thing on or in the second? A wheel is on a bicycle.

what: analogy lesson “Part of a whole”, its trap
text: Another part of the same whole tempts you. For petal, stem is a trap: it is a part too, not the whole.
Made from
Some pairs are a thing and the stuff it is made from. A sweater is made from wool. A window is made from glass.
{A} is made from {B}.
Ask: what would you need to make it? Bread needs flour.
Something that goes with the thing is not what it is made from. Butter goes with bread, but bread is made from flour.
Used for
Some pairs are a thing and the job it does. Scissors cut. A pen writes. A broom sweeps.
{A} is used to {B}.
Say "is used to" between the words. A shovel is used to dig.
Another thing from the same place is a trap. For broom, mop tempts you, but mop is a tool, not a job.

what: analogy lesson “Who does it”, its title
text: Who does it

what: analogy lesson “Who does it”, its idea
text: Some pairs are an action and the person who does it. Someone who bakes is a baker. Someone who sails is a sailor.

what: analogy lesson “Who does it”, its bridge
text: {B} is a person who {As}.

what: analogy lesson “Who does it”, its spot
text: Say "a person who" and the action. A person who paints is a painter.

what: analogy lesson “Who does it”, its trap
text: The thing the person works with is a trap. For bake, bread tempts you, but bread is what a baker makes, not who bakes.
Word families
Some pairs keep the same idea and change the word's job. Decide becomes decision. Brave becomes bravery. Danger becomes dangerous.
{A} becomes {B}: the same idea with a new job.
Look at the ending and the job. If the first pair turns an action into a thing, the second must too.
A word with the same meaning but the wrong job is the trap. For kind to kindness, kindly tempts you, but kindly does a different job.

what: analogy lesson “Stronger and weaker”, its title

what: analogy lesson “Stronger and weaker”, its idea
text: Some pairs are the same feeling or size, turned up. Warm turned up is hot. Hot turned up is scorching.

what: analogy lesson “Stronger and weaker”, its bridge
text: {B} is a stronger {A}.

what: analogy lesson “Stronger and weaker”, its spot
text: Ask: is the second word the same thing, only more so? Tired, then exhausted.

what: analogy lesson “Stronger and weaker”, its trap
text: A near twin at the SAME strength is the trap. Chilly is close to cool, but it is not the far end.

what: the avatar card for Shiva (a Legendary avatar in the Indian Gods / European Gods pack)
text: Shiva is one of the most loved gods in Hinduism, honoured by Hindu families all over the world today. Many families pray to him as the one who protects, changes and makes new beginnings possible. In many homes and temples he is shown in quiet meditation, with the river Ganga flowing from his hair. Many families keep the festival of Maha Shivaratri, a night of prayer, with songs and stories. Every family honours him in its own way — ask yours how they do.

what: the avatar card for Zeus (a Legendary avatar in the Indian Gods / European Gods pack)
text: Zeus was honoured by the people of ancient Greece as the king of their gods, the god of the sky and thunder. They built great temples for him, and the Olympic Games began long ago as a festival held in his honour at Olympia. His stories have been told for thousands of years, and they are still loved and retold today.
